title: Simultaneous Exposure of Tungsten and Tungsten - Rhenium Alloy to Neutron Irradiation and Hydrogen Environment
content: Plasma facing materials (PFM) in fusion reactors are subjected to simultaneous neutron irradiation and hydrogen isotope bombardment. While neutron irradiation effects on tungsten (W) as a PFM have been extensively studied, the synergistic effects of neutron irradiation and hydrogen isotope exposure have rarely been explored. When absorbed in W, hydrogen isotopes dynamically interact with irradiation-induced defects, such as vacancies, which affects their migration and recombination behaviors [1, 2]. This interaction of hydrogen with point defects will subsequently influence the formation and growth of larger defects such as voids and dislocation loops [3, 4]. Consequently, simultaneous exposure to hydrogen isotopes and neutron irradiation may lead to a different defect structure, compared to single irradiation or sequential irradiation followed by hydrogen exposure. The US-Japan collaboration has irradiated various PFM in the High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, including W and W-5% Re alloys [5]. Two types of capsules were irradiated: (1) the hydride capsule, containing vanadium hydride samples, which serves as an in-situ hydrogen source during irradiation, and (2) the reference capsule, which does not contain a designed hydrogen source. This study investigated the synergistic effects of hydrogen exposure and neutron irradiation on hydrogen retention and vacancy behaviors in W and W-5% Re alloys.
